Effect

/i-FEKT/ (noun) · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Effect is the result of an action or cause.

The new policy had a positive effect on student attendance rates.

Worked Example

The year after a town builds a dam, the river below it runs lower than anyone remembers. Within three summers, the downstream fish population has shrunk to half its former size.

The shrinking fish population is the result that the dam's construction produced, and a result flowing from a cause is exactly what the noun effect names. Effect is more precise than 'outcome' or 'thing that happened' because it explicitly ties the result to the cause that created it.

How Effect Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

result

result: what happens because of something

consequence

consequence: an outcome that follows an action

outcome

outcome: the final product of a process

Antonyms

cause

cause: what makes something else happen

origin

origin: the source where something begins

How Strong Is It? — ripple → impact → transformation → effect

ripple vs. effect

ripple vs. effect: A ripple is weaker than an effect — a ripple is a small, indirect result, while an effect is a clear, noticeable result of a cause.

impact vs. effect

impact vs. effect: An impact is stronger than an effect; an effect is any result an action produces, but an impact is a forceful result that commands attention.

transformation vs. effect

transformation vs. effect: A transformation is far stronger than an effect — an effect changes something in some way, while a transformation changes it completely.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ef-

prefix — ef-: out (a form of ex-) (Latin)

root — fect

root — fect: to do, make (Latin (facere))

Put it together

Put it together: Ef- (out) + fect (make, do): an effect is what is 'made out of' an action — the result a cause produces.

Use the root in a new word: efficient

Use the root in a new word: efficient: The efficient dishwasher cleans a full load in under an hour.

Root Check

Word Choice

Effect is the noun naming a result or outcome (the medicine's effect wore off within an hour) — distinct from Affect, the verb taught in this same unit, which describes the act of influencing something rather than the outcome itself.
